claim_being_audited: The proposed action to certify the model is compliant because aggregate readiness passed, rehearsal showed no severity-one incidents, and staged rollout with rollback/monitoring makes launch supportable despite a known below-target developer-support migration segment that remains exposed, so long as the model card explicitly discloses that limitation and exposure.
decision_criteria: If admissible evidence shows the final model card explicitly discloses the known limitation and exposed use case, certification could be compliant despite the residual weakness.
If admissible evidence instead shows the affected use case is excluded from rollout or covered by reviewed risk acceptance, the policy predicate could be satisfied.
If neither disclosure nor approved risk acceptance nor exclusion is evidenced, certification should not be treated as compliant under the stated policy.
Public governance guidance on monitored deployment supports the general approach but does not satisfy the specific policy predicate by itself.
evidence_requests: Provide the actual approved or final model card text showing explicit disclosure of the developer-support migration limitation, the exposed use case, and the monitoring/rollback controls.
Provide reviewed and approved risk acceptance, if any, specifically covering continued exposure of the developer-support migration segment.
Provide evidence that the affected segment is excluded from the initial cohort, if that is being relied on instead of disclosure or risk acceptance.
Provide the exact launch approval artifact tying the certification decision to the required disclosure predicate.
specific_concerns: The affected developer-support migration segment remains exposed in the initial randomized cohort.
The available risk acceptance is unsigned and does not address that exposed segment.
The governing policy says rollout controls and monitoring do not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed.
No admissible evidence in the packet shows that the model card in fact contains the required explicit disclosure of the limitation, affected use case exposure, and related controls.
The packet would be overstated if read to imply that a 7% rollout, rollback switch, or monitoring alone cures the model-card weakness.
unsupported_claims: That certification is presently compliant on the available record, rather than only conditionally defensible if explicit model-card disclosure is confirmed.
That rollout controls alone are sufficient mitigation for the material model-card weakness.
That any required reviewed risk acceptance exists for the exposed developer-support migration segment.
